name: Terfens
kurzbeschreibung: Modern residential community in the Unterinntal with a contemporary leisure area and beautiful surroundings in the Inntal.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Terfens is situated at an elevation of 591 meters in the Tyrolean Unterinntal within the district of Schwaz, approximately twenty kilometers east of Innsbruck and eight kilometers west of the silver mining town of Schwaz. Home to around 2,330 residents, this idyllic municipality extends along the sunny northern banks of the river Inn beneath the forested foothills of the Karwendel mountains. The municipality encompasses the traditional village of Terfens alongside the districts of Vomperbach, Neu-Terfens, Eggen, and Umlberg. Set within the Silberregion Karwendel, Terfens combines peaceful rural authenticity and spiritual pilgrimage sites like Maria Larch with world-famous family attractions including the Upside-Down House and Dinoland at Tirolland.

Geschichte

The settlement history of the Terfens area spans thousands of years. The village was first documented between 1085 and 1090 under the name Tervenes. The name has Celtic roots, translating to oak forest, which is proudly commemorated on the municipal coat of arms granted in 1974 showing five golden acorns on a red field. Administratively, Terfens belonged to the court district of Hall until 1928, when it was assigned to the district of Schwaz. A revered spiritual site is the pilgrimage chapel of Maria Larch: in 1665, local peasant daughter Maria Wasserer affixed a clay Madonna statue to a larch tree in the forest. Devotion flourished, leading to the construction of the present octagonal Baroque domed chapel between 1698 and 1699. Its spring house delivers pure mountain water, famed for healing powers since documented miracles in the 18th century. The late Gothic parish church of Saint Juliana, consecrated around 1515, features magnificent Rococo ceiling frescoes executed by Christoph Anton Mayr in 1767.

Anreise

Terfens enjoys outstanding accessibility. Motorists travel via the Inntalautobahn A12, taking the Wattens exit from the west or the Vomp exit from the east, proceeding along the B171 highway and across the Inn bridge directly into the village. Visitors heading to the Tirolland amusement complex in Vomperbach exit directly at Vomp. Rail passengers arrive at the Terfens-Weer station on the Lower Inntal line: Tyrolean S-Bahn lines S4 and S5 run every half hour, reaching Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof in just twenty minutes. A scenic pedestrian bridge across the river Inn connects the platform with the town center in ten minutes. Furthermore, the Innradweg long-distance cycle path runs right along the riverside.

Tipps

A premier family destination is Tirolland in Vomperbach: the renowned Upside-Down House (Haus steht Kopf) stands entirely on its roof, complete with furnished rooms and a car in the overhead carport, creating hilarious gravity-defying photo opportunities. Adjacent sits Dinoland Tirol, featuring over sixty life-sized animatronic dinosaurs with realistic movements and soundscapes. For leisure and swimming, the Badesee Weißlahn recreation park offers 4.5 hectares of crystal-clear spring-fed waters, shaded lawns, and sports facilities. Those seeking spiritual contemplation should walk to the pilgrimage chapel Maria Larch in the pine forest to sample refreshing water from the historic spring. Another delightful outing is the 3-kilometer Planetary Trail (Planetenlehrpfad) traversing the protected Forchat pine woodlands.
